evidence.mission_note: This is a heavily modified, engine-swapped E30 sedan rather than the documented, mostly-stock 325is the enthusiast-bridge brief calls for; it satisfies the manual-transmission requirement but the undocumented drivetrain swap, Montana title, and likely California registration/smog friction work directly against the low-risk, easily-resalable bridge car the buyer needs given the BMW 335i's unreliability.
evidence.rationale: This listing does not clear the bar for a low-risk enthusiast bridge car: it is a 1985 318i chassis fitted with an undocumented 'rebuilt' S52B32 swap, on a Montana LLC title that has apparently never been registered or smogged in California, with zero receipts for the engine, suspension, or bushing work described in the listing. The 15,000-mile odometer reading is not credible as total mileage on a 41-year-old car with a swapped drivetrain, and no underbody photos or accident history are available to assess rust or prior damage. While the manual Getrag 260 and claimed 3.73 LSD are appealing, and the car photographs as clean and well-presented, the combination of undocumented major work, unresolved title/registration status, and heavy deviation from the desired 'documented, mostly-stock' profile makes this materially riskier and harder to resell than the model's own market notes describe for stock, documented cars. At $16,000 it is priced above an unmodified 325is currently bidding at $11,000 on BaT, without the documentation to justify the premium. This car needs a full PPI plus written answers on titling/smog and build history before it can be seriously considered.
evidence.next_action: Request full documentation (engine rebuild receipts, suspension/bushing install records, any prior state title/Carfax) and clarification on CA smog/BAR referee status; if the seller cannot produce these, decline unless price drops substantially and an independent PPI plus underbody photos can first confirm no structural/rust issues.
